# Semantic Infrastructure Lab

> Building the semantic substrate for intelligent systems

The Semantic Infrastructure Lab (SIL) builds the missing foundation that enables intelligent systems to reason with explicit meaning, not just statistical patterns.

## Quick Navigation

### New to SIL?
Start here to understand what we're building:

- [Founder's Letter](/founders-letter) - Why SIL exists
- [Start Here](/start) - Getting-started guide
- [Project Index](/projects/project-index) - All projects

## Articles

- [Agents That Don't Read Everything](/articles/reveal-subagents): Agents that don't read everything — progressive disclosure for Claude subagents, four production principles
- [Configuration as Semantic Contract](/articles/configuration-semantic-contract): Configuration as a semantic contract between code and environment
- [Find Every Caller in Your Codebase With One Command](/articles/reveal-call-graphs): Call graph queries with calls:// for impact analysis and dead code detection
- [From 15 Files to 500: What Reveal Makes Possible for AI Agents](/articles/reveal-what-it-makes-possible): What reveal makes possible — capabilities and use cases
- [From Filing Cabinets to Agentic Minds: The Long Arc of Information Retrieval](/articles/information-retrieval-history-and-agentic-future): History of information retrieval and the agentic future
- [I Didn't Learn to Trust AI. I Learned to Engineer Trust.](/articles/engineering-trust): Working theory of engineered trust — five properties (observability, verification, containment, continuity, meta-engineering) a human-agent system needs before an imperfect model becomes safe to rely on
- [Inside the Function: Reveal's Fourth Level of Progressive Disclosure](/articles/reveal-inside-the-function): Inside the function — nav flags, control flow, and data flow with reveal
- [Progressive Disclosure for AI Agents](/articles/progressive-disclosure-agents): Progressive disclosure patterns for AI agents
- [Reveal: A Semantic Query Layer for Code, Infrastructure, and Docs](/articles/reveal-introduction): Introduction to Reveal tool
- [Reveal: The Surprising Recipes](/articles/reveal-surprising-recipes): Surprising and powerful reveal recipes and usage patterns
- [Session Archaeology: Excavating Your Claude Code History with `reveal claude://`](/articles/claude-session-archaeology): Article on excavating Claude Code session history using reveal claude://
- [Stop Scrolling. Start Navigating.](/articles/reveal-nav-flags): Navigation flags — stop scrolling, start navigating with reveal
- [The Diff That Shows What Actually Changed](/articles/reveal-diff): Structural diffs with diff:// — what actually changed, not just lines
- [The Hard Part of Agentic AI Isn't Reasoning — It's Grounding](/articles/grounding-not-reasoning): Synthesis of four grounding pillars for token-efficient agents — continuity, doc-finding, progressive disclosure, externalized tasks; reveal CTA
- [The Too-Many-Sausages Problem: A Practitioner's Guide to RFQ Matching at Scale](/articles/rfq-matching-modern-architecture): RFQ matching with modern architecture
- [The Two Halves of Trust Engineering](/articles/two-halves-of-trust-engineering): Each of the five trust properties is engineered twice — once into the agent's operating environment, once into the artifact tooling — and comparing the two exposes calibration as a cross-cutting dimension
- [The Two Speeds of Meta-Engineering](/articles/two-speeds-of-meta-engineering): How a lesson becomes a permanent capability — the three modes of meta-engineering, and why the same loop runs in three hours or seven weeks depending on whether the lesson must travel through someone not currently thinking about it
- [Trained to Please, Empowered to Act](/articles/trained-to-please-empowered-to-act): Thought leadership on agentic AI safety — sycophancy framing, five incidents, permissions vs. contracts
- [Two Commands That Change How You Work With Code](/articles/reveal-pack-and-review): Two commands — pack and review — for code understanding and quality
- [Your Project Has an API Now](/articles/reveal-project-api): Your project has an API now — the full reveal query layer flagship article
